- We have a hard requirement for PHI segregation and auditability (HIPAA).
- Preferred outcome is a private deployment (VPC or on-prem) but procurement is looking for a cost/throughput comparison vs Redwood Dedicated (single-tenant reserved capacity).

Thanks — happy to sync after you share a short worksheet.

Hi Jennifer —

Appreciate the context — this is exactly the kind of input we need. High-level reply first, detailed workbook attached (capacity_workbook_v3.xlsx) + security map draft. Short summary below; full numbers are in the workbook.

Summary (top-level):
- Dedicated (Reserved): 6x A100-80GB (single-tenant pool) with a 2-node burst buffer. Expected steady throughput covers ~80 QPS with plenty of headroom during average hours; designed burst capacity to hit ~160 QPS for short windows via burst nodes and autoscale. Estimated median latency 180–300ms (model dependent).
- Private (VPC or on-prem): On-prem: 5x A100-80GB + 1x management/control node + HSM for keys. For VPC-private (cloud-controlled private): 7x A100-80GB (since we manage some of the infra redundancy). Either private option prioritizes data locality, full audit log access, and HSM integration for key custody.

Key trade-offs:
- Cost: Dedicated reserved is lower operational overhead and faster procurement (no hardware lead times). Private on-prem has higher upfront capital and longer procurement (hardware, racks) but avoids egress and meets the strictest data residency constraints.
- Recovery & SLAs: Dedicated comes with an SLA (we operate replacement and burst fallback). Private on-prem needs a defined runbook for hardware failures; we can include a standby failover path to Redwood Dedicated for emergency tails.

Open questions we used for sizing (please confirm):
1) Which model(s) do you plan to serve? (we sized for a 70B quantized model and a 13B fallback variant — we attached both scenarios)
2) Do you require full offline air-gap (no control plane egress) or will a private VPC with restricted egress suffice?
3) What procurement timeline do you anticipate? (weeks vs months)

I'll loop in Marissa with pricing and Rishi for compliance artifacts. If helpful we can do a 30-minute walkthrough of the workbook.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference

Jennifer — linking some numbers and tradeoffs from our sizing run (extracted from the workbook):

Assumptions used:
- Primary model: Llama2-70B (q4_0 / 4-bit quantized) — serving with Redwood runtime, KV cache enabled.
- Fallback model: Llama2-13B (for cost-sensitive or degraded modes).
- Median prompt/response = 280 tokens; generation length average 120 tokens.

Sizing outputs (conservative):
- Dedicated Reserved (single-tenant):
  - Base pool: 6 x A100-80GB (NVIDIA A100) — supports ~100 sustained QPS at median latency ~230ms for 70B q4_0 with KV cache.
  - Burst: 2 x A100-80GB cold nodes auto-start for peak windows (adds +70 QPS).
  - Network: 100 Gbps aggregation; low-latency interconnect recommended.
  - Storage: 8TB NVMe per node for model shards + fast checkpointing.
  - SLOs: 99.9% availability; p95 latency target < 420ms under typical load.

- Private (on-prem, air-gapped):
  - Base: 5 x A100-80GB + 1x management node (we recommend redundant management if budget allows).
  - HSM: recommended for key custody — Thales/HSM or cloud KMS with on-prem connector depending on vendor.
  - Observability: full log export to customer SIEM; we provide audit pipeline config.
  - SLOs: depends on local ops; we can contract a runbook + optional managed-op SLA.

Operational notes / procurement considerations:
- Time to live: Dedicated reserved: ~2–4 weeks from PO to capacity available. Private on-prem: 10–14 weeks typical (hardware lead times).
- Pricing: Dedicated is Opex (monthly reserved commitment + usage). Private is CapEx + subscription for Redwood Private control plane / support.
- Fallback: recommended to include a cross-deployment fallback (private -> dedicated) for emergency spikes; this requires contract terms around egress and emergency billing.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Confirm model(s) to lock the exact GPU-memory profile.
2) Tell us whether an emergency fallback to Redwood Dedicated is permissible (procurement OKs temporary egress).
3) We'll turn the workbook into a procurement-ready single-page summary + a compliance pack with SOC2 attestations, encryption controls, and an HSM integration checklist.

If it helps, I've included a short table in the workbook with line-item cost bands and procurement-friendly talking points. Happy to hop on a call Friday morning to walk through.

—Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
